rows.summary: Kafka broker-2 is Running/Ready but DNS-isolated from the rest of the cluster (UnknownHostException resolving peer broker hostnames), causing 60 under-replicated partitions. Chaos Mesh was deployed 70 min ago and very likely triggered the ~12-minute-old network disruption that crashed all kafka pods simultaneously. Zero fault-tolerance margin remains; writes are still safe (0 under-min-ISR). Two secondary alerts also firing: Flink checkpoint failures (during the disruption, now recovering) and reconciliation staleness. Escalate to investigate/stop any active Chaos Mesh experiment and fix DNS for broker-2.

Kafka broker-2 (lakehouse-dual-role-2) is running but network-isolated: it cannot resolve the headless DNS names of brokers 0 and 1, causing 60 under-replicated partitions and triggering KafkaBrokerDown. All pods hard-restarted ~12 min ago (exit code 255/Unknown); Chaos Mesh was deployed 70 min ago and likely injected a network fault that left broker-2 isolated. Cluster is still serving writes (0 offline/under-min-ISR partitions) but has zero fault margin. Do NOT restart broker-2 — escalate to investigate the Chaos Mesh experiment.

Broker-2 (lakehouse-dual-role-2) is network-isolated: it is Running/Ready in Kubernetes but cannot resolve other brokers' DNS names, is not being scraped by Prometheus, and is causing 60 under-replicated partitions. A Chaos Mesh experiment deployed ~70 minutes ago and a mass pod-kill ~12 minutes ago are almost certainly the trigger. The cluster is still serving writes (0 offline, 0 under-min-ISR partitions) but has zero margin left.

Flink checkpoint failures are caused by a Flink taskmanager restart ~2 minutes ago (TaskExecutor shutting down event); the job is back RUNNING/STABLE and completing ~25 checkpoints in the last 5 minutes. The alert window will clear as the 10-minute sliding window moves past the restart-induced failures. All infrastructure appears healthy after a broad disruption ~141 minutes ago that also affected Kafka brokers and ingestion pods.
